system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

The Seller’s “[STANDARD]”, “FINAL” and “agreed” labels do **not** establish Buyer acceptance. The recommendations below are buyer-side negotiating positions, not assertions of market practice. They are based on the supplied extracts; the complete SPA and underlying DD documents still require review.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery against the **AUD 24m** price, with separate protection for other claim categories. | **Counter at 100% of price**, with any concession assessed against verified risks and available security; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; exclusions for protected claim categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, aggregating related matters; the draft both excludes smaller losses and permanently deducts AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **36 months** for general warranty notification, with longer category-specific periods and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Seek 36 months and reject automatic extension to all Claims**, avoiding short proceedings deadlines after notification; 18 months may not expose latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title receive the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate protection for capacity, ownership, valid issuance, all shares and freedom from encumbrances. | **Require a separate 100%-of-price cap, no thresholds and at least six years**, subject to appropriate NSW drafting; ownership failure should not be treated as an ordinary business warranty breach. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to **all Claims**; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Preservation of remedies for Seller fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and deliberate concealment, including appropriately attributable conduct. | **Insert an overriding carve-out across every relevant exclusion, cap, threshold and contractual time bar**; Seller must not obtain contractual protection for fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fairly disclosed matters, with enough detail to identify their nature and scope, against identified warranties; a fixed, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and require specific, fair disclosure**, with any general disclosures narrowly agreed; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No knowledge bar; alternatively narrowly defined actual knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without imputation or a duty to investigate. | **Delete the qualifier; use that narrow fallback only if necessary**; constructive knowledge would undermine warranties through hypothetical diligence. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied by delivery of written consent. Final consent and satisfaction of associated conditions are absent. | An effective consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, without unacceptable conditions, adverse variations or unresolved default. | **Make satisfactory consent and satisfaction of its conditions a Buyer-waivable completion condition**, with a long-stop termination right; approximately 30% of FY26 revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release provided **after Completion**. | Repayment and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion, within debt-free/cash-free mechanics. | **Require lender payout evidence and binding discharge arrangements, funded through Completion and deducted from Seller proceeds without double counting**; Buyer should not complete with residual secured-debt exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses treated as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Quantify and include the liability in funds flow/price adjustments, backed by a specific indemnity**, including amounts becoming payable later; omission otherwise leaves Buyer funding a Seller transaction cost. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with payment and assignment evidence absent. | Verified satisfaction of transfer conditions and clear ownership of relevant materials, plus protection for associated title, infringement and remediation losses. | **Require payment verification and a confirmatory assignment at/before Completion, plus a broader standalone indemnity**; paying an invoice alone may not resolve the ownership defect or its consequences. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and unlikely material; possible export of approximately **1,240 records**, with access, scope and notification unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment and legally required notifications, with protection for pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation deliverables and a specific indemnity for resulting lawful costs and liabilities, with completion protection if findings are material**; uncertainty is not proof of either a confirmed breach or immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Review together for timing, scope, commercial necessity, cancellation rights and accounting treatment. | **Reserve treatment pending verification and restrict unapproved commitments**; adjust price or obtain protection only where justified, because neither ordinary-course status nor debt-like treatment is established. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend across all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, payment/adjustment obligations and fraud. | **Rewrite definitions and overriding carve-outs so each regime operates independently**, with only express, appropriate limitations and no double recovery; catch-all wording could nullify negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Harbourglass as 100% holder. | Independent reconciliation of issued shares, ownership history, securities, options, encumbrances and transfer requirements. | **Verify the register against supporting corporate records, searches and transfer documents, with releases and title warranties**; the register is evidence, not a complete clean-title diligence exercise. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranty positions deemed settled under the general regime. | Separate pre-Completion tax protection and robust IP ownership, licensing, infringement and contractor-assignment coverage. | **Reopen both: seek a tax covenant with assessment-aligned survival, generally at least seven years, and tailored IP warranties/indemnities with longer survival and appropriate caps**; an 18-month, 20% general regime inadequately addresses potentially latent liabilities. |

**Completion priorities:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/releases, bonus funding, Ironquay ownership evidence and clean share title. Keep the incident and renewal treatment open until the underlying evidence supports a conclusion.
=== END ADVICE ===
